text:
maria: heads up — canary showed bad behavior when a client connection got requeued and we tried to resume. symptoms: duplicated partial responses + extra billing events. anyone dig into logs?
eli: saw it, i have a trace. TL;DR: resume token collision + router picked a different upstream replica -> KV cache mismatch. short thread below.
jon: can you paste the token/header shape? curious if it's the token or our matching logic.
eli: here's one of the tokens we got: `Resume-Token: v1:rid=svc-42:seq=512:crc=1f3a`
eli: and the router stored resume state keyed by `resume-key = (client-id, session-hash)`; when replica changed the session-hash differed -> we accepted token but replayed from upstream start -> duplicate emission.
tanya: two obvious ops: 1) make resume strictly tied to a cluster-local lease (reject if replica changed), or 2) make resume idempotent at downstream (dedupe by resume-id). tradeoffs: (1) fast and safe but causes more full-replays in failover, (2) more state downstream and complexity.
sam: +1 on listing tradeoffs. note that (2) needs us to keep resume-id tombstones for a TTL -> memory cost and cross-tenant accounting.
maria: proposal draft: router accepts token with 3-tuple (resume-id, offset, checksum). behavior: if resume-id is bound to current upstream session -> fast resume; if resume-id unknown but offset+checksum match upstream snapshot -> best-effort resume; otherwise reject and trigger full-replay fallback. fallback routing: prefer regional replica with closest last-known-session.
jon: how do we surface this to billing? previous incident charged twice. we need a canonical single-claim step.
eli: suggest a token-claim handshake: before unblocking client, router sends a sync to billing: `POST /billing/claim {resume_id, session_id, attempt}`; billing responds 200/409. 409 -> already claimed -> router dedupes emit. will add circuit on that call.
tanya: that adds latency to resume path. can we decouple: allow resume to proceed, but emit a compensating event if duplicate later? refunds are messy.
sam: refunds + customer ops are heavy. preventive dedupe is preferable for enterprise customers. for self-serve maybe async backfill acceptable.
maria: okay. finalizing compromise: default = preventive: router verifies resume-id->session binding; if verification RPC times out, fall back to async mode but mark trace `resume_mode=async_failopen`. enterprise tenants can opt into strict sync-claim mode.
eli: i'll sketch the token change: new token format `v2:rid=<uuid>;sid=<session>;o=<offset>;c=<crc>` and router will check `lease(sid)` on the sessionstore. if lease mismatch -> reject with `x-resume-reject:session-mismatch`.
eli: telemetry: emit counters `resume.attempts`, `resume.fast_path`, `resume.rejected.session_mismatch`, `resume.duplicate_detected`. also histogram `resume.latency` and tag by tenant and `resume_mode`.
jon: billing path: i'll propose two backfills: 1) async refund pipeline keyed on `resume_id` (eventual), 2) sync-claim for enterprise with SLA. will write up options.
tanya: :thinking_face: also add the trace tag `resume_reason` (client-initiated|upstream-failover|requeue) so we can filter incident queries.
maria: action items: eli -> RFC for token v2 + router lease check + telemetry; jon -> billing backfill RFC; tanya -> memory/TTL cost estimates for tombstones and state; sam -> opt-in config for strict vs async resume. sync tomorrow 10:00am PT. @deploy-bot can you reserve a rollback window for canary group? :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: scheduled rollback window: canary=ingress-resume-handler v2, window=2h starting 2023-11-07T22:00:00Z.
eli: i'll add prometheus config snippet now: ```
# metrics
- name: resume_attempts_total
  help: "Total resume attempts"
  type: counter
- name: resume_latency_seconds
  help: "Resume latency"
  type: histogram
```
maria: perfect. also please add correlation key `trace.resume_id` to every emitted span. thanks everyone.
jon: +1, will look at billing paths.
tanya: +1
sam: thanks.
maria: closing for now — see RFC PR when it's up. :rocket:
